audit.whatIsWrong: The entry invents an MR-stacking passive for Galio and treats it as the reason Teemo's poke fails: whys[0] "Galio's passive MR-shield absorbs your level-1 Toxic Shot chip", whys[2] "Galio's MR scaling blunts your poison damage", early "Galio's passive stacks MR from his own items and runes", spikes[0].text "MR-scaling shield absorbs your poison chip", wants.foe[0] "Shield of Durand's MR passive is stacked".
audit.why: Galio's passive is Colossal Smash: 'Every few seconds, Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area.' There is no MR-stacking passive and no MR passive on Shield of Durand — W is a charged defensive stance that shields and then taunts. The correction inverts the advice, because Colossal Smash is a basic attack: Blinding Dart blanks it outright. Telling a Teemo his poison is nullified by phantom resistances makes him play passive in a lane where his blind actually deletes Galio's only auto-attack threat.
audit.corrected: Colossal Smash is an empowered basic attack, so one blind cancels it. What you cannot blind is Winds of War (Q) — an 825-range damage-over-time tornado. Shield of Durand is a charged stance he has to commit to, not a passive resistance stack.
sources: champ-data/_kits/galio.json (P Colossal Smash: 'Every few seconds, Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area', flags autoReset,zone; W Shield of Durand: 'charges a defensive stance, moving slowly. Upon releasing the charge, Galio will taunt', flags hardCC,slow,shield — no MR)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] attributes the knock-up to Q: "Taunt you into his team with W and follow with a Q knock-up to lock you down".
audit.why: Winds of War (Q) is a converging windblast tornado that deals damage over time — it has no displacement. The knock-up is Justice Punch (E), a 650-range dash that knocks up the first enemy champion it meets. Getting the slot wrong here matters because the whole matchup is about respecting the E range, not the Q.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch (E) is the knock-up and the engage; Winds of War (Q) is chip. The order is E in, then W taunt.
sources: champ-data/_kits/galio.json (E Justice Punch: 'briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters', range 650; Q Winds of War: 'two windblasts that converge into a large tornado that deals damage over time')

audit.whatIsWrong: early and whys[1] make Shield of Durand the ranged kill threat: "if you stand at Q range and he has W up, he charges Shield of Durand silently and taunts you"; "Galio can silently stack the W taunt while you try to poke". wants.you[0] also claims blinding before his E means "his dash does zero auto-attack damage mid-flight".
audit.why: Shield of Durand is 275 range. Teemo's auto and Blinding Dart are both 680. Galio physically cannot taunt you from your own spacing, and while charging W he moves slowly, which is the opposite of silent. The real threat is Justice Punch at 650 range closing the gap first. And a blind does not stop Justice Punch: the dash and its knock-up are ability effects, unaffected by blind — the blind's value is cancelling the Colossal Smash auto that follows.
audit.corrected: Outspace the 275-range W entirely; the button that beats your spacing is the 650-range Justice Punch. Hold Blinding Dart for the autos after his E lands, since blind stops neither the dash nor the knock-up.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Q range 680, E Toxic Shot range 680)

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer is built around 'track Justice Punch' and the content around 'respect his E commitment windows', but no cooldown number appears anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7 and Shield of Durand is 18/17/16/15/14, against Blinding Dart's flat 7 seconds. At rank 1 that is one guaranteed free blind per engage attempt and roughly two per W. Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140 — long enough that a roam genuinely costs him lane presence, which is the entry's own level-6 argument but currently unquantified.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch 11s at rank 1 (7s at rank 5); Shield of Durand 18s at rank 1; Hero's Entrance 180s at rank 1. Blinding Dart is a flat 7s, so early on you always have a blind for his engage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing addresses that Teemo has no dash against a champion whose engage can cut him off from terrain.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags 'terrain-cuts-retreat: Galio can cut your retreat with Justice Punch (E) and you have no dash — hold Flash for the wall, not the damage.' Justice Punch steps Galio back and then charges, so he can end up between Teemo and the retreat path. Move Quick is a speed buff, not a blink, and it is cancelled by being struck by an enemy champion or turret — so it does not rescue a Teemo who has already been cut off.
audit.corrected: Move Quick is passive speed that breaks the moment a champion or turret hits you, so it is a spacing tool, not an escape. Once Justice Punch is behind you, Flash is the only out — hold it for the reposition, not for damage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (W Move Quick: 'passively increasing his Move Speed until he is struck by an enemy champion or turret')
champ-data/_kits/galio.json (E Justice Punch: dash, 'briefly step back and charge')

audit.whatIsWrong: mid attributes an MR spike to "a first component (Kindlegem, Blasting Wand)".
audit.why: Neither component gives magic resist — Kindlegem is health and cooldown reduction, Blasting Wand is ability power. The stated cause of the Levels 4-5 stall is simply not a thing.
audit.corrected: The Levels 4-5 stall is a cooldown story, not a resistance story: your Q is rank 2-3 and his Justice Punch is down to 9-10 seconds.
sources: champ-data/_kits/galio.json (no MR in kit); standard item components

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says "your Q is near-maxed" at Levels 4-5.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is rank 2 at level 4 and rank 3 at level 5, maxed at level 9, and it is a flat 7s cooldown at every rank — ranking it produces no spike.
audit.corrected: Q is rank 2-3 at this stage.

audit.why: The packet flags "Shield of Durand's" and "Use Hero's Entrance" as probable wrong ability names. Both are false positives from the near-miss matcher — Shield of Durand and Hero's Entrance are the correct names for W and R. The real error in wants.foe[0] is the phantom 'MR passive' attached to the correct name, and in wants.foe[2] there is no error at all.

edits.before: Galio's passive stacks MR from his own items and runes, meaning your Toxic Shot poison and E damage are partially nullified from the opening seconds — do not expect the same chip-trade dominance you get against a squishy melee. His level-2 W taunt is the kill threat: if you stand at Q range and he has W up, he charges Shield of Durand silently and taunts you into a full Colossal Smash empowered auto combo. Respect the W charge animation and step back the moment you see it; once his W is on cooldown you have a clean window to land Blinding Dart and two poison autos before retreating. Never commit to chasing — Galio's Q poke costs him nothing and he wants you to step forward into taunt range.
edits.after: Galio's passive is Colossal Smash, an empowered basic attack that comes up every few seconds — and because it is a basic attack, one Blinding Dart erases it. What you cannot blind is Winds of War (Q), an 825-range tornado that ticks damage over time, so do not try to win a pure poke war against it. Shield of Durand only reaches 275 units against your 680, so he can never taunt you from your own spacing — the kill pattern is Justice Punch (E) in from 650 range first, then the W taunt on top. That means your blind is reserved for the autos after his E commits, not for the W charge animation. Never step forward to chase; 650 units is exactly the range he wants you at.

notes: champ-data/_kits/galio.json derives no 'knockup' flag for E Justice Punch even though its own description text says 'knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters'.
